arch_mv1329: RULE: Metro Vancouver Regional District, Non-Road Diesel Engine Emission Regulation Bylaw No. 1329, 2021 (saved copy 25 Oct 2026, sources/library/public/mvBylaw1329/full.pdf): s. 1 'emergency engine' means an engine, including emergency generators and other stationary engines, intended for use only in an emergency; 'sensitive receptor' means 'a hospital, an elementary school, a day care facility or a community care facility'; s. 11 emergency engines exempt from Parts 3, 4, 5, 6 and 9; s. 13 discharge 'must not result in: (a) The recirculation of its stack exhaust into the building; or (b) The entrainment of its stack exhaust into surrounding building openings or air ventilation intakes' (no distance); s. 57 (Part 11) 'No person may operate a Tier 0 or Tier 1 engine within 100 metres of a sensitive receptor.' — https://metrovancouver.org/boards/Bylaws/MVRD_Bylaw_1329.pdf
arch_nbc6331: RULE: National Building Code of Canada 2020, Div. B 6.3.3.1.(2) (same in BCBC 2024 and NBC(AE) 2023, local copies): vented products of combustion other than from oil-, gas- and solid-fuel-burning appliances discharged 'not less than a) 2.15 m above sidewalks and driveways, b) 3 m from outdoor air intakes, c) 3 m horizontally or vertically from doors and operable windows, and d) 3 m horizontally or vertically from occupiable outdoor spaces'; Note A-6.3.3.1.(2): occupiable outdoor spaces = occupied >15 min, e.g. main entries, balconies, patios, decks, green roofs, public assembly areas; distances may need to increase for winds and adjacent structures. Application to generator engine exhaust is our reading (?) — data/raw/codes/nbc.txt
arch_nbc6329: RULE: NBC 2020 Div. B 6.3.2.9.(2) and Table 6.3.2.9 (same in BCBC 2024, NBC(AE) 2023): minimum distance of outdoor air intake: truck loading area or dock and bus parking 7.6 m; garage entry/automobile loading 4.5 m; driveway, street, parking space 1.5 m; arterial road 7.6 m; garbage 4.5 m; evaporative heat rejection discharge 7.6 m; sanitary vent 3.5 m; kitchen exhaust 3.0 m; vent for combustion products 3.0 m; intakes >= 0.3 m above roofs/grade. 6.3.1.1.(2)-(3): ventilation per ANSI/ASHRAE 62.1-2016 ss. 6.2-6.5 (Section 5 not referenced) — data/raw/codes/nbc.txt
arch_nbc63215: RULE: NBC 2020 Div. B 6.3.2.15.(5) (evaporative heat rejection systems): discharge away from the building 'not less than a) 2.15 m above sidewalks and driveways, b) 7.6 m from outdoor air intakes, c) 3 m horizontally or vertically from exterior doors and operable windows, and d) 3 m horizontally or vertically from occupiable outdoor spaces'. Applies to cooling towers/evaporative units, not dry air-cooled units — data/raw/codes/nbc.txt
arch_nbc3628: RULE: NBC 2020 Div. B 3.6.2 (same in BCBC 2024, NBC(AE) 2023): 3.6.2.1.(1) fuel-fired appliances in service rooms with 1 h fire separation; (5) equipment using liquid with flash point below 93.3 C in 1 h service room; 3.6.2.2 service equipment subject to explosion incl. some transformers not directly under a required exit; 3.6.2.7.(2) electrical equipment vault 3 h (2 h if sprinklered), solid masonry or concrete, (8) liquid-tight sill >= 100 mm; 3.6.2.8.(1) generator for emergency power for lighting, fire safety and life safety systems in a room with 2 h fire separation containing only the generating set and related equipment — data/raw/codes/nbc.txt
arch_nbc3131: RULE: NBC 2020 Div. B 3.1.3.1 and Table 3.1.3.1 (same values in BCBC 2024, NBC(AE) 2023): fire separations between major occupancies, h: F-2 vs A-1/A-2/A-3/A-4/B/E 2, C/F-2 2 (note 6); F-3 vs A 1, C 1, E 2; D vs A 1, C 1, F-2 3; E vs A 2, C 2 (1 h per 3.1.3.1.(2) where <=2 dwelling units, <=3 storeys); 3.1.3.2.(1) no F-1 in a building with A, B or C; 3.1.3.2.(2) 'Not more than one suite of residential occupancy shall be contained within a building classified as a Group F, Division 2 major occupancy.' — data/raw/codes/nbc.txt
arch_nbc3227: RULE: NBC 2020 Div. arch_nbcDefF: RULE: NBC 2020 Div. A definitions: low-hazard industrial (F-3) combustible content 'not more than 50 kg/m2 or 1 200 MJ/m2 of floor area'; medium-hazard (F-2) more than that and not F-1. Note A-3.1.2.1.(1) examples: A-2 libraries, community halls, schools nonresidential; A-3 'Indoor swimming pools'; C apartments; D 'Laundries, self-service', offices; F-2 'Electrical substations', 'Laundries, except self-service', storage rooms; F-3 'Power plants', storage rooms; no data centre listed. BCBC 2024 3.1.2.8.(1): daycare facility for children = A-2 — data/raw/codes/nbc.txt; data/raw/codes/bcbc2024.txt

arch_vanChildcare: GOVERNMENT GUIDE: City of Vancouver, Childcare Design Guidelines (approved 4 Feb 1993; amended to 19 Jan 2021): s. 1.1(a) avoid or mitigate 'commercial loading or service areas, major mechanical plants', 'building exhaust fans, electrical substations', 'transformers or other noisy, noxious or dangerous uses'; s. 1.1(b) sited away from high-traffic arterials; s. 1.4(a) outdoor play areas 'a minimum of three hours of direct sunlight per day at the winter solstice'; s. 4.2(b) exhaust vents 'should not be located adjacent to outdoor play areas'; s. 4.7(b) rooftop play 'free of skylights, roof vents and/or other mechanical equipment' — https://guidelines.vancouver.ca/guidelines-childcare-design.pdf
